description: This case study is the Chernobyl Forum's assessment of the 1986 Chernobyl accident, a 55-page second revised version that summarises 2003 to 2005 studies by UN agencies, the World Bank and the governments of Belarus, the Russian Federation and Ukraine. It has three assessments, on health consequences (an expert group coordinated by WHO), environmental consequences (coordinated by IAEA) and socio-economic impact, followed by recommendations on health care and research, environmental monitoring, remediation and research, and economic and social policy. Its summary reports more than 600,000 registered emergency and recovery workers, over 5 million residents of contaminated areas with relatively low doses, more than 4,000 childhood thyroid cancers diagnosed by 2002, and that mitigation such as evacuation reduced exposures. Access: free PDF download from the IAEA site; no licence is stated in the text. Coverage is the three most affected countries. Caveats: only the summary and contents were read, and the numbers are those of the 2005 assessment. It suits emergency response and recovery planning studies of nuclear accidents, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Chernobyl's Legacy: Health, Environmental and Socio-Economic Impacts and Recommendations to the Governments of Belarus, the Russian Federation and Ukraine (Chernobyl Forum 2003-2005, second revised version)
outcomes: The Forum reviews the health, environmental and socio-economic consequences twenty years on: emergency workers and on-site personnel received the highest doses, more than 600,000 people were registered as emergency and recovery workers, over 5 million residents of designated contaminated areas received doses not much above natural background, more than 4,000 childhood thyroid cancers had been diagnosed by 2002, and evacuation and other measures substantially reduced exposure. It ends with recommendations on health care, environmental monitoring and remediation, and economic and social policy.
